issues.reason: The light-verb/event-noun rule states that an event-noun's witness IS the eventuality ("the ceremony occurred in March" — tense and Time go directly on it), so the accident witnesses are eventualities and the event oblique Location ("in/at/on …") fits; the entity bar applies only where "there is no eventuality for Location to attach to", and the objection cannot single out Location while the reviewer's own notes accept Past and Time on that same symbol.

The per-member rule of Cardinality/Quantifiers presupposes a reified group EVENT to distribute (its conclusion is an event bundle over a Skolem event term), which the light-verb route removes here — the members are themselves the events — so no licensed rule shape exists and the omission is the coverage gap the reviewer itself files, not a defect.

gaps_confirmed: the light-verb/event-noun rule is written for a singular event-noun and says nothing about a plural/group of event-nouns — where Past/Time/Location attach and whether they distribute
"recently" is not among the listed speech-anchored deictic constants, so a bare Time symbol for it is an unstated (if natural) extension
new_gaps: "many" in a counting use: it is listed among the proportion words that set strength, and is absent from the vague-quantity lexicon ("a few / several / dozens / a lot of"), so its canonical CardinalityPhrase string is unspecified
notes: Both issues restate the same uncovered construction (plural event-noun under a light verb); every emitted atom is true of the sentence and well-typed, so the calibration line accepts the improvisation.
